  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],

  "anova_plan": [
    "Perform a One-Way ANOVA for each of the five response variables (Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) with Stimulation Paradigm as the fixed factor.",
    "For 'Success', verify normality assumptions; if violated, consider a transformation (e.g., arcsine square root) or a non-parametric alternative (Kruskal-Wallis) as a robustness check.",
    "For 'Path Efficiency', note the wide range (0.0009 to 29.8) and potential skewness; check residuals for homogeneity of variance before proceeding with standard ANOVA.",
    "Test the null hypothesis that the mean performance metric is equal across all five stimulation paradigms for each variable."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If any ANOVA yields a significant F-statistic (p < 0.05), conduct post-hoc pairwise comparisons.",
    "Use Tukey's Honestly Significant Difference (HSD) test for all pairwise comparisons to control the family-wise error rate.",
    "Specifically compare 'Sham' against all other paradigms to identify the magnitude of the deficit in the control group, given the large mean difference observed in the summary data.",
    "Compare 'ICMS Only' and 'Dim Visual Only' against 'Combined' to determine if the combined approach yields superior performance."
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Apply Tukey's HSD correction for all post-hoc pairwise comparisons to maintain the family-wise error rate at alpha = 0.05 across the set of comparisons derived from the ANOVA tests.",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Since the response variables are continuous (except Success which is binary/0-1) and the predictor (Stimulation Paradigm) is categorical, Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression with dummy coding is appropriate for modeling Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and AD. For the 'Success' variable, which is binary (0 or 1), a Logistic Regression model is explicitly recommended over linear regression to ensure predicted probabilities remain within [0, 1] and to model the log-odds correctly.",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence of observations: Verify that trials are independent within and between mice.",
    "Normality of residuals: Check Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests for residuals of each ANOVA model.",
    "Homogeneity of variances: Perform Levene's test or Bartlett's test for equal variances across the five paradigm groups.",
    "Linearity: Not applicable for ANOVA, but relevant for the regression component regarding the relationship between dummy-coded paradigms and continuous outcomes.",
    "For 'Success': Check for separation issues in logistic regression if any paradigm has a success rate near 0 or 1."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Significant differences are expected in 'Time-to-Target' and 'Success', with 'Sham' showing the highest mean Time-to-Target (4.68s) and lowest Success rate (0.27) compared to other groups.",
    "Significant differences are expected in 'Path Efficiency' and 'Average Speed', with 'Sham' showing lower efficiency (0.31) and speed (10.74) than 'Combined' (0.50, 12.83).",
    "Significant differences are expected in 'AD' (Angular Dispersion), with 'Sham' showing lower dispersion (0.24) than 'Combined' (0.40), suggesting less variability or tighter clustering in the control group, contrary to typical 'error' metrics.",
    "The 'Combined' paradigm is hypothesized to yield the best overall performance (lowest Time-to-Target, highest Success, highest Efficiency/Speed) based on the summary means."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "The dataset contains 76,655 rows, but the distribution of samples across paradigms is highly imbalanced (Combined: 48,846 vs. Sham: 3,505), which may affect the power of the ANOVA for the smaller groups and the stability of the regression coefficients for 'Sham'.",
    "The 'Path Efficiency' variable has a very wide range (0.0009 to 29.8), suggesting potential outliers or a non-normal distribution that may violate ANOVA assumptions.",
    "The 'Success' variable is binary; treating it as a continuous variable in ANOVA (as suggested by the summary stats) is statistically suboptimal compared to logistic regression.",
    "Potential confounding variables such as specific mouse IDs (8 levels) are not included in the primary ANOVA design, though they should be considered in a mixed-effects model to account for inter-subject variability."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a Linear Mixed-Effects Model (LMM) for the continuous variables (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) and a Generalized Linear Mixed-Effects Model (GLMM) with a binomial link for 'Success', including 'Mouse' as a random intercept to account for repeated measures and individual subject variability, followed by post-hoc pairwise comparisons with Tukey correction."
}
